subject.title: fix(opencode): public models work without API keys

question: Should OpenClaw support anonymous OpenCode Zen requests for currently free-priced models despite upstream and OpenClaw documentation requiring Zen login, billing setup, and an API key?
rationale: Free pricing does not establish a stable no-auth provider contract, and this PR deliberately bypasses the existing authorization boundary for user prompts; maintainers must decide the supported product and privacy posture.

options.title: Require an upstream anonymous-access contract
options.body: Keep the PR blocked until OpenCode documents no-key access for these exact API endpoints and models, then align OpenClaw docs and tests with that contract.

options.title: Keep Zen API-key authenticated
options.body: Close or narrow the change and retain the current onboarding/API-key path for all OpenCode Zen models.

options.title: Sponsor a temporary experimental path
options.body: Explicitly accept the volatility and privacy trade-off, label/document the anonymous path as experimental, and define its removal behavior.

recommendation.title: Require an upstream anonymous-access contract
recommendation.body: Keep the PR blocked until OpenCode documents no-key access for these exact API endpoints and models, then align OpenClaw docs and tests with that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: A provider-auth product decision spans the OpenCode extension and core auth contract rather than a mechanical contributor repair.
